title: HTTP, REST, and API design fundamentals
intro: This module builds the vocabulary every Web API interview assumes: how HTTP messages flow through ASP.NET Core, how REST names resources, which status codes to return honestly, how to version without breaking clients, how OpenAPI documents contracts, and how idempotency keys plus cache headers keep APIs correct under retries and cheap under read load.

conceptCards.title: HTTP fundamentals
conceptCards.summary: Request = method + URL + headers + body. Response = status + headers + body. ASP.NET Core exposes one HttpContext per exchange through Kestrel.
conceptCards.example: GET /api/orders?status=open with Authorization and X-Correlation-Id headers

conceptCards.title: REST principles
conceptCards.summary: Resources are nouns in URLs. HTTP methods are verbs. Servers are stateless — auth rides on every request.
conceptCards.example: POST /api/orders → 201 Created with Location header, not POST /createOrder

conceptCards.title: Methods and status codes
conceptCards.summary: Safe GET, idempotent PUT/DELETE, non-idempotent POST. Use 4xx for client faults, 5xx for server faults — never hide errors in 200 bodies.
conceptCards.example: 409 Conflict for duplicate idempotency key; 422 for declined payment

conceptCards.title: API versioning
conceptCards.summary: URL, header, or query strategies each trade visibility vs cache behavior. Ship v2 alongside v1; sunset with metrics.

conceptCards.title: OpenAPI and Swagger
conceptCards.summary: Machine-readable contract for docs, client generation, and CI diff. Document all status codes including 4xx.
conceptCards.example: ProducesResponseType(409) + Swagger UI Bearer JWT scheme

conceptCards.title: Idempotency and caching
conceptCards.summary: Idempotency-Key prevents duplicate charges on retry. ETags enable 304. Cache-Control directs browsers and CDNs.
conceptCards.example: Redis idempotency:abc → replay 201; ETag RowVersion → 304 Not Modified
